subject.name: Adam Dąbrowski
subject.disambiguation: Robotics software engineer and CTO of Robotec.ai, Warsaw. Not the researchers of the same name in signal processing, space engineering or medicine.

about: Every factual claim made on adamdbrw.github.io, with sources. status: 'verified' = an independent public source confirms the claim; 'self-reported' = stated by Adam (site, LinkedIn, speaker bios he supplied) and not independently published; partial corroboration is listed in evidence. Notes disclose relationships between Adam and the authors of some sources.
how_to_verify: Start with the ids in start_here: the strongest independently verified claims.
Open each evidence URL; the 'shows' field says what to look for.
GitHub authorship: commits, pull requests and issues are by the account adamdbrw (also older commits authored as 'Adam Dąbrowski' or 'adamdbrw').
Commit ranks change over time; they are given with the date read.

claims.claim: Since 2018 his work has been taken up beyond his own company: the micro-ROS requirements (2018), the optimised SQLite recording defaults in ROS 2's rosbag2 (2021), the ROS Simulation Interfaces (shipped by Gazebo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim) and REP 158 (lead author; accepted by the ROS and Gazebo PMCs).

evidence.shows: micro-ROS chapter cites his OFERA requirements report as first author (see micro-ros)
rosbag2 SQLite defaults merged into ROS 2, 2021 (see rosbag2)
Gazebo implements the Simulation Interfaces (see simif-implementations)
NVIDIA Isaac Sim uses the Simulation Interfaces (see simif-implementations)
REP 158 lists him as first author (see rep158-author, rep158-accepted)

claims.note: Summary of the claims micro-ros, rosbag2, simif-implementations, rep158-author and rep158-accepted.

claims.claim: Lead author of REP 158, 'OpenUSD Conventions for Simulation Asset Interoperability in Open Source Robotics', with co-authors from Robotec.ai, NVIDIA and Ekumen.

evidence.shows: Official REP page: 'By Adam Dabrowski (Robotec.ai), Mateusz Zak, Michal Pelka (Robotec.ai), Ayush Ghosh, Renato Gasoto (NVIDIA), Franco Cipollone (Ekumen)'; Status: Accepted
Pull request adding the REP draft (merged June 2026)
Core schema, pull request by adamdbrw
He asked the MuJoCo team for feedback on REP 158 (June 2026)

claims.claim: REP 158 was accepted by the Gazebo PMC (28 September 2026) and the ROS PMC (29 September 2026) and marked Accepted on 22 October 2026.

evidence.shows: ROS PMC minutes: REP 158 passes
Gazebo PMC minutes: REP 158 vote
Status change to Accepted, by adamdbrw

claims.claim: REP 158 has a public, Apache-2.0 compliance checker (ros-usd-check, shipped as OpenUSD validators) in ros-simulation/openusd-schemas, built by the Robotec.ai team (commits by Mateusz Żak and Maciej Majek).

evidence.shows: Compliance checker source, one module per REP section

claims.claim: Proposed the standardisation of ROS simulation interfaces (November 2024).

evidence.shows: Issue 'Standardization of simulation interfaces' opened by adamdbrw on 5 Nov 2024; Gazebo lead thanks him for kicking it off

claims.note: Addisu Z. Taddese (GitHub azeey), Gazebo lead maintainer, replied on 15 November 2024: 'Thanks @adamdbrw for kicking this off. I do agree that having a standardized simulation interface would be good for the community.'

claims.claim: Lead author of the ROS Simulation Interfaces: wrote the first version (pull request #1: all 33 commits, squash-merged into one; 185 review comments from 13 reviewers, among them Gazebo and ROS maintainers), then developed them with NVIDIA contributors; most of the non-empty lines in the 38 interface definition files today are his: 72% by default git blame, 77% ignoring whitespace (-w), 83% also following moved and copied lines (-w -C) (November 2026), and he created 29 of the 38 files; listed as author and maintainer.

evidence.shows: First pull request, by adamdbrw (opened 17 Dec 2024, merged 21 Mar 2025); reviews include Gazebo maintainers (azeey, scpeters)
ROS Index lists Adam Dąbrowski as maintainer and author
Repository: run git blame on the msg, srv and action files. Commit counts understate his share because pull request #1's 33 commits were squash-merged into one commit.

claims.claim: The ROS Simulation Interfaces are implemented in Gazebo, NVIDIA Isaac Sim and O3DE, and released for ROS 2 Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical and Rolling.

evidence.shows: Gazebo documentation for the interfaces
'Implement ROS standard simulation interfaces', by azeey (Gazebo lead maintainer), merged 30 September 2025
Isaac Sim tutorial: simulation control through the standard simulation_interfaces package
O3DE documentation for the interfaces
ROS Index: releases for Humble, Jazzy, Kilted, Lyrical and Rolling

claims.note: The O3DE implementation is by Robotec.ai; Gazebo and NVIDIA Isaac Sim implemented the interfaces themselves. Gazebo's implementation (gazebosim/ros_gz#790, September 2025) was written by its lead maintainer, Addisu Z. Taddese.

claims.claim: More than 60 public GitHub repositories outside Robotec.ai declare the ROS Simulation Interfaces as a dependency (November 2026). About ten are simulators or simulator bridges, among them the MVSim simulator, OmniSim, community bridges for Genesis and Newton, and PyBulletFleet; others include the toolkit of the AI for Industry Challenge and its entrants' copies, and coursework.

evidence.shows: MVSim simulator: its ROS 2 node implements the Simulation Interfaces
AI for Industry Challenge toolkit: its engine uses the Simulation Interfaces
OmniSim: a Simulation Interfaces node
Genesis bridge (community, 200+ stars): a dedicated gs_simulation_interfaces package
Newton bridge (community) implements the Simulation Interfaces
Newton bridge announcement; the author chose the Simulation Interfaces so users need not learn Newton's API
Gazebo's ros_gz implementation

claims.note: Count from a GitHub code search for simulation_interfaces in package.xml files, excluding Robotec.ai and the package's own repository; the search needs a GitHub login, so the listed files are the checkable sample.

claims.claim: Presented the new ROS simulation standard at ROSCon 2025 with Ayush Ghosh (NVIDIA).

evidence.shows: Talk video, 'Introducing the new ROS simulation standard'

claims.claim: Conceived and designed Slingshot (2026), Robotec.ai's product that turns a site scan into a simulation-ready digital twin with OpenUSD output; wrote about 95% of the code (reconstruction with Gaussian splatting, people removal, camera calibration, object extraction, OpenUSD export) with an AI coding-agent harness he built; its OpenUSD exports are checked against REP 158.

evidence.shows: Public product page: a digital twin of a site from a scan, with OpenUSD output

claims.note: The product is public; the source repository is private, so his share of the work and the REP 158 check are his own statements.

ROS 2 Galactic release notes: in a 200 Mbps stress test the Foxy release dropped up to 70% of messages, Galactic retained about 100%.

claims.note: MCAP has been rosbag2's default storage since ROS 2 Iron; the SQLite plugin and the options remain.
